title: ～おかげで — thanks to ～
summary: Gives the cause of a good result, with a feeling of gratitude: “thanks to ～.” It follows a noun + の or a plain-form clause. The result is something favorable that has already happened.

patterns.gloss: noun + のおかげで (先生のおかげで)
plain form + おかげで (手伝ってくれたおかげで)

body.p: As in 先生のおかげで合格できた, it gives the reason for a good result while thanking a person or situation. Nouns take の, and verbs and adjectives take the plain form (na-adjectives take な, and nouns in the past take だった).
For the cause of a bad result, use せいで. おかげで is basically for good results. It can be used ironically for a bad result (あなたのおかげで遅れた), but then it is blame, not thanks.

examples.ja: 先生（せんせい）のおかげで、試験（しけん）に合格（ごうかく）できました。
examples.romaji: Sensei no okage de, shiken ni gōkaku dekimashita.
examples.tr: Thanks to my teacher, I was able to pass the exam.

examples.ja: 天気（てんき）がよかったおかげで、遠（とお）くの山（やま）まで見（み）えた。
examples.romaji: Tenki ga yokatta okage de, tōku no yama made mieta.
examples.tr: Thanks to the good weather, we could see all the way to the distant mountains.
examples.note: Plain past form + おかげで.

examples.ja: みんなが手伝（てつだ）ってくれたおかげで、引（ひ）っ越（こ）しが早（はや）く終（お）わった。
examples.romaji: Minna ga tetsudatte kureta okage de, hikkoshi ga hayaku owatta.
examples.tr: Thanks to everyone helping, the move finished quickly.
examples.note: A natural pair with 〜てくれた.

pitfalls: Do not forget の with nouns: × 先生おかげで, ○ 先生のおかげで.
For a bad result use せいで. Using おかげで for one sounds sarcastic.
